name: Light Greenish Blue
lede: Light greenish blue is a plain description more than a name: old color dictionaries use the phrase to define aqua, horizon blue and cerulean blue.

sections.title: A phrase that defines other names
sections.body:
Paterson uses "light greenish blue" as a definition for several names: aqua blue, horizon blue and aqua itself [1][2]. Cerulean blue is described as a vivid pigment of that hue, made from chromium, cobalt and tin oxides and first made in 1860 by George Rowney and Son [3]. Glaucous is given as a light greenish blue or sea-green [4].

So the phrase works like a bracket around a stretch of the color wheel, with no single object behind it [1][3][4].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch here, #63F7B4, is closer to a minty green than the blues the dictionary describes [5]. Its nearest named neighbors are [[aquamarine]], [[seafoam-green]] and [[aqua]] [5]. For the pigment, see [[cerulean-blue]]; for the sea-grey sense, see [[glaucous]] [3][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No usable archive measurements exist for this name, so there is no painting data to quote [5].
